newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-UNHERALDED BASTIA BIDDING FOR EUROPEAN BERTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNHERALDED BASTIA BIDDING FOR EUROPEAN BERTH.

text.p: Less than five years after a stand collapsed at their Furiani stadium killing 17 people, unheralded Bastia have become the sensation of French soccer and are bidding for a place in next season's European Champions' League.
In May 1992, Corsican football was in a state of shock after disaster struck before a French Cup match against Marseille.
Now Bastia, who beat Nancy 2-0 on Saturday, lie third in the first division with a game in hand on the two sides above them. They are just one point behind wealthy Paris St Germain.
And the Corsicans could go above PSG if the French League upholds their claim that they should be awarded three points for the postponement of their match at Caen.
The match, scheduled for February 14, was called off because of a flooded pitch and was not re-scheduled within 24 hours as French league rules state it should be.
If Bastia are awarded a full three points they would be just four points behind leaders Monaco.
Coach Frederic Antonetti says he had not expected such a fine season.
"Our first goal was to remain in the first division. Then we aimed at Intertoto berths, now our direct objective is a European Cup spot," he said.

Bastia's performance is all the more surprising as the club, whose best past result was reaching the UEFA Cup final in 1978, have one of the lowest annual budgets in the first division at around 47 million francs ($8.5 million).
Despite their limited resources, they have managed to attract talented foreign players like Slovakian Lubomir Moravcik and Yugoslav striker Anto Drobnjak.
There have been many scandals and tales of fraud and tax evasion in Bastia's history but president Francois Nicolai said it belonged to the past.

"People must stop believing that we go to the Swiss border with suitcases full of beautiful banknotes which we hand out to our players. All that sort of stuff is finished," he told sports daily l'Equipe.
"For us, each victory is another brick to rebuild our old stadium."
